content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a guide in 2009 addressing water, cleaning, and disinfection of facilities. This guide aims to assist airport and aircraft operators, as well as other responsible entities, in achieving high standards of hygiene and sanitation to protect travelers. 2. In 2011, WHO released the Guide to Ship Sanitation, 3rd Edition, which emphasizes the public health significance of ships in relation to disease transmission and highlights the importance of implementing appropriate control measures. 3. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and WHO jointly published guidelines in 2003 for characterizing microbial hazards in food and water. These guidelines provide a structured framework to assist governmental and research scientists in assessing microbial risks. 4. WHO's 2006 publication, Health Aspects of Plumbing, describes the processes involved in designing, installing, and maintaining effective plumbing systems. It also addresses microbial, chemical, physical, and financial concerns associated with plumbing. 5. A 2003 publication by WHO, edited by J., evaluates the role of heterotrophic plate count (HPC) measurements in managing drinking-water safety and their significance for water quality and human health. 6. WHO's 2007 publication on Legionella provides an overview of the sources, ecology, and laboratory detection of Legionella bacteria. It includes risk assessment and management strategies for environments susceptible to Legionella, as well as outbreak management policies and practices. 7. In 2018, WHO published guidance on managing radioactivity in drinking water. This document supports radionuclide management in both emergency and non-emergency situations. 8. WHO's 2002 publication, authored by M. Sobsey, reviews methods and systems for household water collection, treatment, and storage, aiming to improve water supply and accelerate health gains. 9. The 2019 WHO report critically examines the occurrence of microplastics in the water cycle, including tap and bottled drinking water. It evaluates potential health impacts from microplastic exposure and discusses their removal during wastewater and drinking-water treatment processes. 10. A 2004 WHO publication, edited by J., provides guidance on the distribution, transmission routes, and infection risks of pathogenic environmental mycobacteria in water. It also offers strategies for controlling these pathogens in water and other environmental settings. 11. WHO's 2012 publication on pharmaceuticals in drinking water offers evidence-based guidance and recommendations for managing pharmaceutical contaminants in water supplies. 12. The 2017 WHO publication on potable reuse highlights aspects of reusing municipal wastewater for drinking water. It provides guidance on risk assessment and management to ensure the safety of drinking water derived from treated wastewater. 13. WHO's 2006 publication, edited by O. Schmoll et al., analyzes hazards to groundwater quality and their potential risks to specific water supplies. It serves as a tool for developing strategies to protect groundwater for health by managing drinking-water source quality. 14. A 2003 discussion paper by the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment of the Netherlands explores the concept and methodology of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) as a public health metric, particularly for assessing drinking-water quality. 15. WHO's 2016 publication synthesizes knowledge on quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA) to support its application in water safety management, including water supply, reuse, and recreation, with a focus on managing risks from fecal pathogens. 16. The 2011 WHO handbook provides practical guidance for rapidly monitoring drinking-water quality and safety using statistical methods, sanitary surveys, and field approaches. 17. WHO's 2006 publication reviews evidence on the potential transmission of avian influenza (H5N1) through water and sewage. It also discusses ways to reduce risks to human health. 18. A 2009 WHO text supports the Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality by providing data on Cryptosporidium. It assists authorities in setting health-based targets and water suppliers in determining the required performance of water treatment processes. 19. WHO's 2011 publication on desalination highlights health risks associated with different desalination processes. It provides guidance on risk assessment and management to ensure the safety of desalinated drinking water. 20. The 2004 WHO publication, edited by R. Ainsworth, addresses microbial contaminants and the growth of microorganisms in piped water distribution systems. It offers practices to ensure drinking-water safety in such systems. 21. WHO's 2009 publication examines the scalability of household water treatment systems, reviewing their development and evolution, identifying constraints, and recommending ways forward. 22. The 2021 WHO publication on toxic cyanobacteria in water provides background information and practical guidance for assessing and managing risks from cyanobacteria and their toxins in drinking and recreational water bodies. 23. WHO's 2017 publication on turbidity offers information on its uses and significance, targeting regulators and operators of drinking-water supplies. 24. The 2001 WHO publication, edited by L. Fewtrell and J. Bartram, provides guidance on microbial water quality and health issues. It is intended for environmental and public health scientists, water scientists, policymakers, and those responsible for developing standards and regulations. 25. WHO's 2014 publication on water safety in distribution systems serves as a reference tool for water suppliers and regulators familiar with the water safety plan approach. It aims to enhance risk assessment, management, and investment planning for water distribution systems. 26. The 2009 WHO manual on water safety plans provides step-by-step guidance for developing and implementing water safety plans through 11 learning modules, each representing a key step in the process. 27. WHO's 2012 publication offers step-by-step guidance for planning, designing, and implementing water safety plans for rural and remote communities, including those with piped schemes and point sources. 28. The 2005 WHO publication on water safety plans provides guidance on preventive management, control, and monitoring of drinking-water quality from catchment to consumer. 29. A 2004 WHO publication critically analyzes the removal and inactivation of pathogenic microbes in water. It serves as a tool for water quality specialists and design engineers in decision-making regarding microbial water quality. 30. WHO's 2004 publication on waterborne zoonoses is an invaluable tool for professionals assessing and managing diseases caused by microorganisms of animal origin that also infect humans.
